heroHeadline: Philippines Extends Thitu Island Runway for Potential F-16 Operations as China's Scarborough 'Marine Nature Reserve' Protest Awaits Response — Reed Bank Standoff Day 5, Three Fronts Active
heroSubtitle: Satellite imagery analyzed by Radio Free Asia and EurasiaReview confirms the Philippines is extending the Rancudo Airfield runway at Thitu Island (Pag-asa) by ~200 meters over previously submerged land — a ₱1.65B ($29M) project assessed as potentially enabling F-16V combat aircraft operations from Philippines' largest Spratly outpost for the first time. Alongside a new sheltered harbor at Lawak Island (₱1B, $18M), the infrastructure upgrades signal a deliberate Philippine strategy to shift Spratly deterrence from passive garrison posture to active forward-basing capability, consistent with the country's $5.5B F-16V acquisition approved April 2025. An F-16V stationed at Thitu would be within combat radius of China's Fiery Cross, Subi, and Mischief Reef bases (~160 nm), cover Second Thomas Shoal (~50 nm) and Reed Bank (~70 nm), and directly challenge China's current tactical air dominance over the central South China Sea. China has not yet issued a formal protest targeting the satellite imagery reports. Simultaneously, the Reed Bank standoff entered Day 5 on May 12 as China's research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33 continues survey operations near Iroquois Reef, ~85 nm from Palawan, with no public response to the Philippines' May 11 UNCLOS Article 246 note verbale. The Philippines DFA diplomatic protest over China's Scarborough Shoal 'marine nature reserve' declaration also remains unanswered — the third escalatory Chinese measure at Scarborough in five weeks (April 10-11 floating barrier, May 9 CCG Chuanshan training, May 2026 reserve claim). Former SC Justice Antonio Carpio warned the reserve mirrors China's civilian-to-military conversion playbook at Fiery Cross and Subi Reefs. Three concurrent SCS confrontations persist: Reed Bank, Second Thomas Shoal (BRP Sierra Madre garrison), and Scarborough. Vietnam separately added ~534 acres of reclaimed land in the Spratlys over the past year (Bloomberg May 9), with 15 harbors and 3 new ones under construction at Grierson, Petley, and South Reefs — underscoring the SCS infrastructure competition accelerating across multiple claimants.
